notes.body: The son meets his father's two-horned charge — traitor if the stranger is true, fool if he is false — with a two-horned reply: across these forty years you were either a knower who withheld it from me, or an ignorant man who needed the stranger even more than I did. Every door the charge leaves open, the reply closes. But it did not work as a logic trap; it worked because gentleness, honesty, and forty years of love had prepared the ground, so the old man could finally admit what he had been waiting to admit.
notes.quote: Consider these forty years I have stood beside you

notes.body: Abu Malik calms the panicked community with the lost camel of the believer: wisdom is the believer's own lost property, and if you spot your lost camel in a stranger's hands, you don't reject it because of who is holding it — you reclaim it. So if these converts really carry an increase in knowledge, that knowledge is owed back to you. They are not a rival to fear but your own property to go and recover.
notes.anchor: wisdom is the believer's lost camel
notes.quote: knowledge is the lost property of every believer

notes.body: The outer word and the inner meaning are one single deposit, released together in one act of inspiration — think of the outer text as sheet music and the inner sense as the master musician who knows how it is meant to be played. The higher one brings the book; the lower one carries the living interpretation, and he invents no new notes. Text without the musician is a corpse, rigid lifeless legalism; the musician without the text is a wraith, where anyone can claim it means anything.
notes.anchor: sheet music and the master musician
notes.quote: Each is from God — both the sending down and the interpretation

notes.body: Why do the learned sit as if no living witness exists? Every age is opened by three working together: a rebellious devil who makes falsehood attractive, a stubborn tyrant who makes opposition costly, and a hypocritical scholar who dresses submission up as piety. None can do the job alone — temptation without force fades, force without legitimation gets overthrown, legitimation without temptation has nothing to dignify. The scholar's part is to give the tyrant's violence a religious face; that is how the marks of prophethood get cut off in nation after nation.
notes.quote: a rebellious devil, a stubborn tyrant, and a hypocritical jurist
